text:
Who is Momma?

'Momma', or Officio Commissar Ballasorna Markova, was well known for her particularly effective, efficient, and loyal Bullgryn and Orgyn companies. Their only blemish on their combat record was on Koron XII where during a battle with chaos Ballasorna was injured and written off as dead by imperial forces as her part of the trench was overrun. The boneheads amongst Ballasorna's troop heard the order to fall back over vox net and initially obeyed the command... only for them to return with all ogryns formally under the commissar's command from across the battlefield to break rank and push through the daemon battlelines. The titanic headbutt of force broke the chaos center and pushed to the overwhelmed dugout, eyewitnesses reported hearing dozens of voices crying out for 'momma' as they mercilessly shattered the chaos host. in the end the combined mass of gryns managed to reclaim Ballasorna's position, literally pulling her from the jaws of a daemon prince to do so. Ballasorna perished from her wounds not long later. Commissar Ballasorna's 212th Abhuman Company would forever be known as Bella's Big Boys and continue to serve in her name with marked distinction and honor. Boneheads in the 212th have been retrofitted with a shoulder mounted vox box playerthat broadcasts recorded reminders recovered from Ballasorna's affects. The reminders, as well as the simple nudge of 'momma wouldn't like that' or 'momma said', motivate and encourage Ballasrona's 'boys' while going about their ordered work. Curiously, units attached to the 212th have also reported that they quite enjoy the lullabies that sometimes are sung from the vox boxes despite no 'lullabies' or anything of the sort having been found in the recordings upon initial screening.

text:
Technically this isn't a work song. A work song has a rhythm that shows you the pace of the labor and where the work puts extra exertion

This song has a bunch of those hard punches but they're too irregular to be a work song since those tend to punch on either 2s or 4s

This song is a type of spiritual called a field holler. Yes it was sung while working, but 'work song" has a specific meaning. A field holler can be recognized by its sustained drone, drifting rhythm, and narrative focus

Fun fact; the theme from Spongebob is technically a work song. His name is the spot where you pull.
"Who lives in a pineapple under the sea? 1-2 1-2 Absorbent and yellow and porous is he 1-2 1-2" 
This is because sea shanties are work songs. Not to be confused with sea songs which are typically either laments or jigs/reels (the difference between these is the timing one is a 6-beat the other is a 4-beat). A dirge is a type of lament specifically for a funeral. Interestingly there was a name for a field holler on a ship. It's called a Capstan shanty, while the work song was a Halyard (Haul-yard) shanty. The Capstan was most commonly sung while walking the anchor wheel. So if you're trudging you now know what you're singing

This is an absolute banger, by the way. Reminds me a lot of the song O Death
